1	/**
2	 * Consumer views: the rows a patient-facing chart application shows for one patient's record at one
3	 * health organization.
4	 *
5	 * Each organization publishes record items ({@link FolioItem}). For each organization a mapper implements
6	 * {@link Transform}: it receives every item that organization published for one patient (in any order,
7	 * including superseded and retracted items) and a local date `asOf` (`YYYY-MM-DD`), and returns
8	 * {@link ViewRows}: the organization's record as it stood at the end of that day. A view the organization has
9	 * nothing for is an empty array.
10	 *
11	 * Rules shared by every view:
12	 *
13	 * - **As-of.** An item counts when its `recorded` time is on or before the end of `asOf` (23:59:59.999 local
14	 *   time). Among those, an item does not count if a counting item supersedes it (directly or through a chain:
15	 *   if C supersedes B and B supersedes A, A is replaced too) or retracts it. A superseding or retracting item
16	 *   recorded after `asOf` has no effect yet. `supersedes` and `retracts` only refer to items of the same issuer.
17	 * - **Corrections versus changes.** Supersession replaces an item entirely (correction, amendment, re-statement).
18	 *   A retracted item was entered in error and is treated as if it never existed. A change in clinical state (a
19	 *   medicine paused, a problem resolved) arrives as a new fact in a new item, not as a supersession; the
20	 *   earlier item still counts as history.
21	 * - **Time zone.** The consumer's time zone is America/Chicago. "Local date" and "local time" mean wall-clock
22	 *   time there. Convert date-times that carry an offset or zone to local time (e.g. `2025-03-04T03:30:00Z` is
23	 *   local date 2025-03-03, 21:30). A date-time with no offset and no zone is already local time: report it as
24	 *   written, never shift it and never drop it. A plain date is a local date.
25	 * - **Partial dates.** A source date may be only a year (`2019`) or a year and month (`2019-06`). Keep exactly
26	 *   the precision the source has; never pad to a full date.
27	 * - **Only what this organization records.** Report what this organization's items say, without inference from
28	 *   other organizations and without correcting the source. Rows come from structured payload entries; the
29	 *   narrative may help interpret an entry, but is never the only basis for a row.
30	 * - **Evidence.** Every row lists the items (and, where the payload has them, entry ids) it rests on; at least
31	 *   the item that gives the row its current state.
32	 * - **Sensitive entries.** Report everything, including entries the organization marks restricted or
33	 *   confidential. Tag rows with `sensitivity` when the source marks the entry with a sensitive category (map
34	 *   the source's own category) or when the entry plainly belongs to one (e.g. sertraline for depression →
35	 *   `mental-health`). Never drop a row because it is sensitive; whether to show or share it is the patient's
36	 *   later decision.
37	 * - **Determinism.** Same input, same output. No clock, randomness, network or file access.
38	 */
39	
40	/**
41	 * One record item as published by a health organization. Items are never edited; corrections arrive as new
42	 * items that supersede or retract earlier ones.
43	 */
44	export interface FolioItem {
45	  /** Record-item format identifier. Carries no clinical meaning. */
46	  folio: string;
47	
48	  /** Identifier of this item, unique within the issuer. Referenced by `supersedes`, `retracts` and row evidence. */
49	  id: string;
50	
51	  /** The organization that published the item. All items given to one transform call share the same issuer. */
52	  issuer: string;
53	
54	  /** The patient the item is about, as identified by the issuer. */
55	  patient: string;
56	
57	  /**
58	   * When the clinical event happened (visit, specimen collection, list review…). Date or date-time, possibly
59	   * partial. Not used for the as-of cut-off.
60	   */
61	  effective: string;
62	  /** End of the clinical event when it spans a period (e.g. a hospital stay). */
63	  effective_end?: string;
64	
65	  /**
66	   * When the organization committed the item (date-time). Decides whether the item counts for a given `asOf`:
67	   * it counts when this is on or before the end of `asOf`, local time.
68	   */
69	  recorded: string;
70	  /** Who wrote or signed the item, as far as the issuer says. */
71	  author?: { id?: string; name?: string; role?: string };
72	
73	  /**
74	   * The organization's own schema that types `payload`: its location, the type name within it, and the
75	   * SHA-256 of the schema document.
76	   */
77	  schema?: { url: string; type: string; sha256: string };
78	
79	  /**
80	   * Ids of earlier items of the same issuer that this item replaces entirely (correction, amendment,
81	   * re-statement). Transitive. The replaced items no longer count once this item counts.
82	   */
83	  supersedes?: string[];
84	
85	  /**
86	   * Ids of earlier items of the same issuer that were entered in error. Nothing replaces them; once this item
87	   * counts, they are treated as never having existed.
88	   */
89	  retracts?: string[];
90	
91	  /**
92	   * Human-readable Markdown account of the item. `<ref id="…">` spans point at payload entries. May help
93	   * interpret an entry; never the only basis for a row.
94	   */
95	  narrative: string;
96	
97	  /** Structured entries, typed by the organization's schema (`schema`). Rows are built from these. */
98	  payload: Record<string, any>;
99	}
100	
101	/**
102	 * The mapper's entry point. `items`: every item one organization published for one patient, in any order,
103	 * including superseded and retracted ones. `asOf`: a local date `YYYY-MM-DD`. Returns that organization's
104	 * record as it stood at the end of `asOf` (America/Chicago). Must be deterministic.
105	 */
106	export type Transform = (items: FolioItem[], asOf: string) => ViewRows;
107	
108	/** All rows for one organization, one patient, one as-of date. Each array is empty when there is nothing. */
109	export interface ViewRows {
110	  /** Outpatient (home) medicines, one row per drug ingredient. */
111	  medications: MedicationRow[];
112	  /** Conditions the patient has or had, one row per condition. */
113	  problems: ProblemRow[];
114	  /** Current substances to avoid because of a past reaction. */
115	  allergies: AllergyIntoleranceRow[];
116	  /** Laboratory results for the listed analytes, one row per result. */
117	  labs: LabResultRow[];
118	  /** Clinic and hospital vital-sign sets and home readings. */
119	  vitals: VitalRow[];
120	}
121	
122	/**
123	 * A local date with the precision the source has: `YYYY`, `YYYY-MM` or `YYYY-MM-DD`. Never padded
124	 * (a source saying "June 2019" gives `2019-06`, not `2019-06-01`).
125	 */
126	export type PartialDate = string;
127	
128	/**
129	 * The items a row rests on. Must include at least the item that gives the row its current state; may
130	 * include earlier items it also relies on (e.g. the start of a medicine that is now held).
131	 * `item_id`: the item's `id`. `entry_id`: the id of the payload entry within that item, when it has one.
132	 */
133	export type Evidence = { item_id: string; entry_id?: string }[];
134	
135	/**
136	 * Sensitive categories. `mental-health`: psychiatric conditions and their treatment (e.g. depression,
137	 * sertraline). `substance-use`: alcohol, opioid or other substance use disorders and their treatment
138	 * (e.g. buprenorphine). `sexual-reproductive-health`: contraception, pregnancy, fertility, sexual health.
139	 * `hiv-sti`: HIV and other sexually transmitted infections and their treatment (e.g. chlamydia, an
140	 * antiretroviral). `genetic`: genetic test results and inherited conditions (e.g. a BRCA1 variant).
141	 * Set when the source marks the entry with such a category (map the source's own category) or when the entry
142	 * plainly belongs to one. Omit when none applies.
143	 */
144	export type Sensitivity = 'mental-health' | 'substance-use' | 'sexual-reproductive-health' | 'hiv-sti' | 'genetic';
145	
146	/**
147	 * One outpatient (home) medicine. Hospital-only orders (infusions, drugs given only during a stay) are not
148	 * rows; a discharge prescription for home use is.
149	 *
150	 * One row per drug ingredient. If the source has several lines or orders for the same ingredient over time,
151	 * report the most recent one: the one whose own latest event (start, change, hold, resume, stop) is latest.
152	 * A line or order entered in error never existed. Stopped medicines that the source still shows are rows.
153	 *
154	 * Snapshots versus events: if the source publishes its medication list as repeated snapshots (each item a
155	 * full list), the latest counting snapshot is the list, and a drug absent from it is not reported. If the
156	 * source publishes events or status changes per line, the latest event for a line decides its state, however
157	 * old that event is.
158	 *
159	 * If a patient's own list names the same drug twice with conflicting statuses, report one row for it; which
160	 * entry wins is not specified.
161	 */
162	export interface MedicationRow {
163	
164	  /**
165	   * Generic ingredient name, lower case, without salt or dosage form; brand names translated
166	   * (e.g. "Ventolin HFA" → "albuterol", "amoxicillin trihydrate 500 mg capsule" → "amoxicillin").
167	   * Omit only when the record does not say which drug it is.
168	   */
169	  ingredient?: string;
170	
171	  /**
172	   * RxNorm code of the ingredient (term type IN), only when the source itself states an ingredient-level
173	   * code. Never looked up or derived from a product-level code.
174	   */
175	  rxnorm_ingredient?: string;
176	
177	  /** The medicine's name as the source writes it (e.g. "Ventolin HFA 90 mcg/actuation inhaler"). */
178	  drug_name: string;
179	
180	  /**
181	   * - `active`: the patient should be taking it (clinician record) or says they are taking it (own list).
182	   * - `held`: paused, with intent or possibility of resuming; not taking now. Distinct from stopped.
183	   *   On a patient's own list, an entry marked as taken but annotated by the patient as paused or stopped
184	   *   for the time being is held.
185	   * - `stopped`: discontinued.
186	   * - `unknown`: listed with no decision recorded (e.g. a list the source marks as not reviewed).
187	   */
188	  status: 'active' | 'held' | 'stopped' | 'unknown';
189	
190	  /**
191	   * Local date the current status began, per the source: the hold date for held, the stop date for stopped,
192	   * the start or resume date for active. Source precision. Omit if unknown.
193	   */
194	  status_since?: PartialDate;
195	
196	  /**
197	   * Amount per administration currently prescribed; for held or stopped rows, the amount at the time of the
198	   * hold or stop. On a patient's own list, the amount the patient says they take.
199	   * - Strength per unit and a count: report the mass (strength × count): "ibuprofen 200 mg, take 2 tablets"
200	   *   → 400 mg; "albuterol 90 mcg/puff, 2 puffs" → 180 mcg.
201	   * - No count but a time ("take in the evening") means one unit: "cetirizine 10 mg tablet, take in the
202	   *   evening" → 10 mg.
203	   * - `tablet` only when the strength is unknown ("1 tablet of prednisone", strength not given → 1 tablet).
204	   * - Normalize unit spellings: "milligrams" → mg; "µg", "mcg", "micrograms" → mcg; "U", "IU", "unit(s)" →
205	   *   units; "ml", "cc" → mL; "tab(s)" → tablet.
206	   * - Omit when there is no single amount: a range ("1–2 puffs"), a sliding scale, an amount that depends on
207	   *   a condition, or a strength with no directions at all.
208	   */
209	  dose?: { value: number; unit: 'mg' | 'mcg' | 'units' | 'mL' | 'tablet' };
210	
211	  /**
212	   * QD once daily; BID twice daily (also "every 12 hours"); TID three times daily (also "every 8 hours");
213	   * QHS once daily at bedtime; QW once weekly; PRN as needed (e.g. "every 6 hours as needed for wheeze");
214	   * other for any other schedule (four times daily, every other day, monthly, tapering). A once-daily direction
215	   * given only as "nightly" or "at night" may be QHS or QD. Omit when the source gives no frequency.
216	   */
217	  frequency?: 'QD' | 'BID' | 'TID' | 'QHS' | 'QW' | 'PRN' | 'other';
218	
219	  /**
220	   * Only for stopped rows, and only when the source gives a coded or clearly stated reason.
221	   * `adverse_reaction`: stopped because of a side effect or reaction (e.g. rash on amoxicillin).
222	   * `ineffective`: did not work. `therapy_changed`: replaced by another drug or regimen.
223	   * `course_complete`: a planned course ended (e.g. a 10-day antibiotic course). `patient_choice`: the
224	   * patient decided to stop. `other`: a stated reason that fits none of these.
225	   */
226	  stop_reason?: 'adverse_reaction' | 'ineffective' | 'therapy_changed' | 'course_complete' | 'patient_choice' | 'other';
227	
228	  /** The source's free-text reason for the current status, as written (e.g. "holding until after knee surgery"). */
229	  status_reason_text?: string;
230	
231	  /** true for the patient's own account (a self-reported list); false for a clinician's record. */
232	  patient_reported: boolean;
233	
234	  /** true when the source says the medicine was bought without a prescription (over the counter). Omit otherwise. */
235	  otc?: boolean;
236	
237	  /** Sensitive categories of this medicine; see {@link Sensitivity}. Omit when none applies. */
238	  sensitivity?: Sensitivity[];
239	  /** Items and entries this row rests on; at least the one giving the current status. */
240	  evidence: Evidence;
241	}
242	
243	/**
244	 * A condition the source asserts the patient has or had. One row per condition: entries that restage or
245	 * recode the same condition are one row with the latest wording, codes and stage.
246	 *
247	 * Not rows: ruled-out conditions; conditions only suspected (working, provisional, "rule out") and never
248	 * confirmed; diagnoses recorded only to bill an encounter, unless the source says its problem list is built
249	 * that way.
250	 *
251	 * A diagnosis the source attributes to a drug (a named drug, a drug class, or an "adverse effect of <drug>"
252	 * code) also yields an {@link AllergyIntoleranceRow} for the drug. "Urticaria due to amoxicillin" gives a
253	 * problem row for urticaria and an allergy row for amoxicillin. A code that names only the adverse effect and
254	 * no condition (e.g. ICD-10-CM T36.0X5A "adverse effect of penicillins") gives the allergy row alone.
255	 */
256	export interface ProblemRow {
257	
258	  /** The condition in the source's latest wording (e.g. "Moderate persistent asthma"). */
259	  condition: string;
260	
261	  /** ICD-10-CM code as the source states it in its latest entry (e.g. "J45.40"). Omit if not given. */
262	  icd10cm?: string;
263	
264	  /** SNOMED CT concept id as the source states it in its latest entry. Omit if not given. */
265	  snomed?: string;
266	
267	  /** `active`, or `resolved` when the source says resolved, inactive-resolved or historical. */
268	  status: 'active' | 'resolved';
269	
270	  /**
271	   * When the condition began, per the source, as a local date with the source's precision
272	   * (`{ value: "2019-06", precision: "month" }`). Omit if unknown.
273	   */
274	  onset?: { value: PartialDate; precision: 'year' | 'month' | 'day' };
275	
276	  /**
277	   * Chronic kidney disease rows only: the KDIGO GFR category the source most recently recorded, as recorded
278	   * by a clinician (from wording, a code, or a category field). Never computed from lab values. Omit otherwise.
279	   */
280	  ckd_stage?: 'G1' | 'G2' | 'G3a' | 'G3b' | 'G4' | 'G5';
281	
282	  /**
283	   * Chronic kidney disease rows only: the KDIGO albuminuria category the source most recently recorded, as
284	   * recorded by a clinician (from wording, a code, or a category field). Never computed from lab values.
285	   * Omit otherwise.
286	   */
287	  albuminuria?: 'A1' | 'A2' | 'A3';
288	
289	  /** Sensitive categories of this condition; see {@link Sensitivity}. Omit when none applies. */
290	  sensitivity?: Sensitivity[];
291	  /** Items and entries this row rests on; at least the one giving the latest wording and status. */
292	  evidence: Evidence;
293	}
294	
295	/**
296	 * A current entry on the list of substances to avoid because of a past reaction. Makes no claim about
297	 * mechanism. Only current entries: inactive, refuted or entered-in-error entries are not rows, and
298	 * "no known allergies" is not a row.
299	 *
300	 * Also produced from a drug-attributed diagnosis (see {@link ProblemRow}). The substance is then the specific
301	 * drug when the record names it; when it names only a drug class, the one drug of that class on the patient's
302	 * medication list in the same item if there is exactly one (class "penicillins", amoxicillin on the list →
303	 * amoxicillin), otherwise the class as written.
304	 */
305	export interface AllergyIntoleranceRow {
306	
307	  /**
308	   * For a single drug: generic ingredient name, lower case ("Keflex 500 mg" → "cephalexin"). For anything
309	   * else (drug classes, combinations, foods, environmental substances): as written ("Sulfonamide
310	   * antibiotics", "Peanut", "Latex").
311	   */
312	  substance: string;
313	
314	  /** RxNorm ingredient code, only when the source states an ingredient-level code. Never guessed. */
315	  rxnorm_ingredient?: string;
316	
317	  /**
318	   * Decided by what happened, not by which list the source keeps the entry on and not by mechanism.
319	   * - `hypersensitivity`: hives, rash, swelling of lips/face/tongue, anaphylaxis, bronchospasm, whatever
320	   *   the mechanism.
321	   * - `side_effect`: a predictable, non-dangerous effect that made the drug unacceptable (e.g. stomach upset
322	   *   on erythromycin, drowsiness on an antihistamine).
323	   * - `serious_adverse_event`: serious harm attributed to the drug that is not a hypersensitivity-type
324	   *   reaction (e.g. liver injury on isoniazid, pancreatitis on valproate).
325	   * If the source keeps everything on one undifferentiated list, decide from the recorded reaction.
326	   */
327	  reaction_type: 'hypersensitivity' | 'side_effect' | 'serious_adverse_event';
328	
329	  /**
330	   * `immune` only when the source (or a confirmed allergy test it records) says the reaction is immune-mediated;
331	   * `non_immune` when known not to be (well-established non-immune drug effects, e.g. nausea on erythromycin);
332	   * `unknown` when not established. Use `unknown` when in doubt.
333	   */
334	  mechanism: 'immune' | 'non_immune' | 'unknown';
335	
336	  /** The source's reaction wording, several manifestations joined with "; " (e.g. "hives; lip swelling"). */
337	  reaction?: string;
338	
339	  /**
340	   * `high`: re-exposure could be serious or life-threatening; `low`; `unknown` when the source gives neither.
341	   * Map a source's severity scale by meaning: mild → low; severe or life-threatening → high.
342	   */
343	  criticality: 'low' | 'high' | 'unknown';
344	
345	  /** When the reaction first occurred, local date with the source's precision. Omit if unknown. */
346	  onset?: { value: PartialDate; precision: 'year' | 'month' | 'day' };
347	
348	  /** Sensitive categories of this entry; see {@link Sensitivity}. Omit when none applies. */
349	  sensitivity?: Sensitivity[];
350	  /** Items and entries this row rests on; at least the one giving the current entry. */
351	  evidence: Evidence;
352	}
353	
354	/**
355	 * Reported analytes and their fixed units (`LabResultRow.unit`). Convert source values to these units.
356	 *
357	 * | analyte         | meaning                                      | unit          |
358	 * |-----------------|----------------------------------------------|---------------|
359	 * | `creatinine`    | serum/plasma creatinine                      | mg/dL         |
360	 * | `egfr`          | estimated glomerular filtration rate         | mL/min/1.73m2 |
361	 * | `potassium`     | potassium                                    | mmol/L        |
362	 * | `sodium`        | sodium                                       | mmol/L        |
363	 * | `chloride`      | chloride                                     | mmol/L        |
364	 * | `bicarbonate`   | bicarbonate (total CO2)                      | mmol/L        |
365	 * | `anion_gap`     | anion gap                                    | mmol/L        |
366	 * | `bun`           | urea nitrogen                                | mg/dL         |
367	 * | `glucose`       | laboratory glucose (not a home meter)        | mg/dL         |
368	 * | `a1c`           | hemoglobin A1c, NGSP                         | %             |
369	 * | `uacr`          | urine albumin/creatinine ratio               | mg/g          |
370	 * | `platelets`     | platelet count                               | 10*3/uL       |
371	 * | `wbc`           | white blood cell count                       | 10*3/uL       |
372	 * | `hemoglobin`    | hemoglobin                                   | g/dL          |
373	 * | `bhb`           | beta-hydroxybutyrate                         | mmol/L        |
374	 * | `ph`            | pH                                           | [pH]          |
375	 * | `pco2`          | partial pressure of CO2                      | mmHg          |
376	 * | `lipase`        | lipase                                       | U/L           |
377	 * | `troponin`      | troponin I                                   | ng/mL         |
378	 * | `cholesterol`   | total cholesterol                            | mg/dL         |
379	 * | `triglycerides` | triglycerides                                | mg/dL         |
380	 * | `hdl`           | HDL cholesterol                              | mg/dL         |
381	 * | `ldl`           | LDL cholesterol, measured or calculated      | mg/dL         |
382	 *
383	 * 10*3/uL is thousands per microlitre: 350 000 cells/uL is 350. Other analytes are not reported.
384	 */
385	export type Analyte =
386	  | 'creatinine' | 'egfr' | 'potassium' | 'sodium' | 'chloride' | 'bicarbonate' | 'anion_gap' | 'bun'
387	  | 'glucose' | 'a1c' | 'uacr' | 'platelets' | 'wbc' | 'hemoglobin' | 'bhb' | 'ph' | 'pco2' | 'lipase'
388	  | 'troponin' | 'cholesterol' | 'triglycerides' | 'hdl' | 'ldl';
389	
390	/**
391	 * One laboratory result for a listed analyte ({@link Analyte}).
392	 *
393	 * One row per result. A result shown several times (copies in several items, a preliminary then a final copy)
394	 * is one row, taken from the copy with the most advanced status; its evidence lists the copies used.
395	 *
396	 * Only values that stand. Leave out results withdrawn, invalidated or corrected away by the lab; results of
397	 * orders voided or entered in error; results not performed; superseded copies. A confirmation repeat on a
398	 * new measurement is a second valid result and its own row.
399	 *
400	 * eGFR: one row per calculation the source reports for a specimen. When the source reports variants of one
401	 * calculation with and without a race coefficient, report only the one without. Report the value as printed;
402	 * never recompute.
403	 */
404	export interface LabResultRow {
405	  /** Which analyte; see the table on {@link Analyte}. */
406	  analyte: Analyte;
407	
408	  /** Numeric value in the analyte's unit, converted if the source used another unit. ">90" → 90. */
409	  value: number;
410	
411	  /** The comparator printed with the value (">90" → `>`). Omit for plain values. */
412	  comparator?: '<' | '>' | '<=' | '>=';
413	
414	  /** The analyte's fixed unit from the table on {@link Analyte}, written exactly as there (e.g. "mg/dL", "[pH]"). */
415	  unit: string;
416	
417	  /**
418	   * Specimen collection time, RFC 3339 with offset (e.g. `2025-03-04T08:15:00-06:00`). If the source gives a
419	   * date-time without offset, it is local time: keep the wall-clock time and add the America/Chicago offset in
420	   * effect then.
421	   */
422	  collected: string;
423	
424	  /** `final` (including amended or corrected values that stand) or `preliminary`. */
425	  status: 'final' | 'preliminary';
426	
427	  /**
428	   * eGFR rows only: the equation the source says it used (CKD-EPI 2021 race-free, CKD-EPI 2009, MDRD);
429	   * `unknown` if not stated. Omit for other analytes.
430	   */
431	  egfr_equation?: 'ckd-epi-2021' | 'ckd-epi-2009' | 'mdrd' | 'unknown';
432	
433	  /** LOINC code of the result as the source gives it. Omit if not given; never looked up. */
434	  loinc?: string;
435	  /** Items and entries this row rests on; at least the copy the row's value and status come from. */
436	  evidence: Evidence;
437	}
438	
439	/**
440	 * A vital-sign set or a home reading.
441	 *
442	 * A clinic or hospital vital-sign set (measurements taken within a few minutes at one visit) is one row; a
443	 * repeat blood pressure later in the same visit goes in `repeat_*`. Each home reading is its own row. Each
444	 * measurement is reported once: a hand-entered reading that duplicates a device reading taken a minute or two
445	 * earlier with the same values is one row, preferring the device copy.
446	 */
447	export interface VitalRow {
448	
449	  /** `clinic`; `hospital` (emergency department or inpatient); `home` (patient's own devices). */
450	  setting: 'clinic' | 'hospital' | 'home';
451	
452	  /**
453	   * Local wall-clock time `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM` in America/Chicago. For a clinic or hospital set: the time of its
454	   * first blood pressure, or of its first measurement if it has no blood pressure. For a home reading: the
455	   * reading's time. Times without offset are already local: report as written.
456	   */
457	  local_time: string;
458	  /** Systolic blood pressure (first reading of the set), mmHg. */
459	  systolic_mmhg?: number;
460	  /** Diastolic blood pressure (first reading of the set), mmHg. */
461	  diastolic_mmhg?: number;
462	
463	  /** Systolic pressure of a repeat blood pressure later in the same visit, mmHg. Clinic/hospital sets only. */
464	  repeat_systolic_mmhg?: number;
465	  /** Diastolic pressure of a repeat blood pressure later in the same visit, mmHg. Clinic/hospital sets only. */
466	  repeat_diastolic_mmhg?: number;
